Hi Mina —

Thanks for sending over the updated Order Form and the proposed MSA bundle. We ran this past our legal team and they asked for a couple of clarifications around the publicity / reference language before procurement can sign. The key asks are: 

- Helix needs an explicit carve-out that prevents Redwood from using Helix logos or press quotes for any public marketing without a separate written approval for each use.
- If Redwood requests a case study or joint press, Helix wants a 15 business day review window and the right to redact any confidential technical details.
- We are ok with a limited reference listing ("customer" on website) but no logos in third-party collateral or social posts unless approved.

Attached is a marked-up Order Form (we highlighted the publicity paragraph). Can you confirm whether the MSA language supports a per-request approval flow (instead of a standing marketing permission)?

If necessary, we can have our counsel propose precise alternative language — looped CC'd is Mark (our procurement lead).

Thanks,
Tina

Hi Tina — thanks for the quick read and the marked-up Order Form. I appreciate the specificity on the approval windows.

Short answers up front: yes, we can accommodate a per-request approval requirement; we generally ask for a limited, non-exclusive marketing permission so we don't have to chase signatures for small references (e.g., "Customer: HelixHealth" in a customers page), but we are fine gating logo use and case studies behind explicit sign-off.

I'm looping in Dev (legal ops) and Marissa (AM lead) to propose exact redline language that balances Helix's control over logos with Redwood's need for lightweight references.

Next steps I propose:
- Dev to circulate two alternative clauses: (A) narrow permission for name-only references on Redwood website and sales decks (no logo); (B) per-request approval required for press releases, logos, and quotes with a 15 business day review.
- If Helix accepts (A)+(B), we can re-issue the Order Form redline and attach to the MSA as an amendment.

I'll hold the O/F in pending signature until we agree.

Subject: RE: Order Form / MSA - publicity clause questions

Thanks Mina / Tina — attached is a proposed redline for the MSA publicity section and a short comment sheet. High level: we can accept Helix's per-request approval for logos and press releases, plus the 15 business day review, with two guardrails:

1) We request a standing permission for "name-only" references limited to one-line listing on Redwood's customer page and in sales collateral (no logo, no detailed quotes). Language: "Customer may be listed by name on Provider's website and in Provider's sales materials, provided Provider does not use Customer logos or Customer confidential information without prior written approval."

2) For case studies/press releases/logos/quotes: "Provider will not use Customer's logo, trade dress, or customer quotes in marketing or press materials without Customer's prior written consent, which Customer will not unreasonably withhold; Customer will provide approval or comments within fifteen (15) business days of submission, failing which approval will be deemed granted."

Note on the bolded clause: Helix asked for the ability to redact technical details — that can be captured in the approval process (we accept edits redacting confidential technical content). We prefer the "deemed granted" fallback to avoid indefinite blocking; if Helix cannot accept deemed grant, we can change to "no later than 30 days" as a hard stop.

Attachment: publicity_clause_proposals.docx (docx, 68KB)

CC: Marissa — customer is stickier on brand use, so please advise if you want to escalate to marketing.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Legal Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Tina Morales <tina.morales@helixhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Order Form / MSA - publicity clause questions

Dev — thanks for the clear options. Helix Legal and Procurement are aligned with per-request approvals for logos and quotes. A few points from our side:

- We cannot accept an automatic "deemed granted" if the submission contains any confidential technical content that would require redaction. For purely marketing copy/quote approvals we can accept a deemed silence after 15 business days.
- We will accept a one-line name-only listing on your website (no logo) as described.
- We also require that any co-branded assets be mutually approved in writing prior to publication.

Proposed compromise language we will accept: 

"Provider may list Customer's name on Provider's website and in Provider's sales materials; any use of Customer logo, co-branded assets, press releases, or customer quotes shall require Customer's prior written approval. For non-technical marketing copy, Customer shall provide approval or comments within fifteen (15) business days of submission, after which approval shall be deemed granted. For submissions that include Customer confidential technical information, Customer shall provide a response within fifteen (15) business days and may withhold or condition approval as reasonably necessary to protect such confidential information."

If you are ok with that split approach (deemed grant only for non-technical marketing copy), Helix will sign the Order Form and we can execute via DocuSign.

Thanks — I have attached an example banner we cannot accept without separate approval so you can see the logo placement concern.

Tina
Tina Morales
